text:
Tyler Seguin is in the last year of his contract, and Yahoo Sports passed along an insider report this week that he and the Stars haven't started extension talks. That's the backdrop for a season that has been all chances and no finish: three goals in 25 games, none in his last 14.

The underlying numbers say he's due, loudly. He has 6.4 expected goals, an individual chance rate of 1.04 per 60 that's well above last season's 0.61 over 27 games, and a 5.4% shooting percentage against a talent range closer to 12.5%. Dallas has also scored 5.6 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice. Very little of this looks like decline.

He's playing under 15 minutes a night now, mostly as a middle-six piece with power-play time (four of his eight points). Glen Gulutzan said he sees Seguin's speed returning after his shootout winner in Vegas on November 19, per a Dallas Hoops Journal headline, but NHL EDGE has his top speed in the 28th percentile. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a strong setup man last season, though over just six games. Watch the shooting percentage; a few goals would change the contract conversation fast.
